claims.text: As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at approximately 1000 °C.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance and undergoes pesting in air.
The proposed intervention is substitutional microalloying with approximately 2 at.% Al.
Adding approximately 2 at.% Al will improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Approximately 2 at.% Al will promote formation of a thin, continuous, adherent Al2O3 surface scale on equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Al has a strong affinity for oxygen and will preferentially oxidize during high-temperature exposure.
Preferential oxidation of Al will form a stable alumina layer under the proposed exposure conditions.
The alumina scale will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion and retard further oxidation and pesting.
The Al addition and resulting scale will preserve the microstructural characteristics responsible for ductility and strength.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, the Al-modified alloy will have markedly lower oxidation weight gain than untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, the Al-modified alloy will exhibit a protective, adherent alumina layer.
The room-temperature tensile ductility of the Al-modified alloy will remain comparable to that of untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The approximately 1000 °C yield strength of the Al-modified alloy will remain comparable to that of untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed protection is expected to apply to cast material exposed to air near 800 °C for approximately 5 hours.
Performance under longer exposures, different temperatures, or different atmospheres remains unestablished.
